sections.h2: Which Erie County office handles what
sections.html:
Erie County divides the work. City and town assessors set values, town tax receivers collect current bills, and the county's Real Property Tax Services (RPTS) office handles delinquent county tax and foreclosure.

OfficeWhat it handlesContact
City and town assessorsAssessed valuesListed on the county's General Information page
Town tax receiversCurrent tax bills outside BuffaloAsk the town clerk for collection dates and the penalty schedule, which differ by municipality
RPTSDelinquent county tax, foreclosure, online lookup and paymentRath County Office Building, 95 Franklin Street, Room 100, Buffalo, NY 14202; (716) 858-8333
County ComptrollerSurplus money left after a foreclosure auction pays the taxes and charges on a parcel(716) 858-8400

The county's Pay Your Taxes page takes current City of Buffalo county property taxes and delinquent Erie County taxes for any town or city in the county, and lets you look up what is owed. If you live outside Buffalo, current tax goes to your town receiver.

sections.h2: How Erie County forecloses on unpaid tax
sections.html:
The county can foreclose on a tax lien once it has gone unpaid for two or more years, using a numbered in rem proceeding. In Rem 173 covered liens through tax year 2022, and the county filed its List of Delinquent Taxes with the County Clerk on September 9, 2025. A statutory foreclosure fee of $500 had to accompany the unpaid liens. A later round, In Rem 174, began on May 5, 2026. Call RPTS for the status of that round and the next sale schedule.

  • Pay with cash, certified check, bank check or money order. Personal checks are not accepted.
  • Interest is applied on the first day of each month, so the payoff figure changes monthly.
  • Paying old liens does not stop later years from becoming eligible, so open 2023, 2024 and 2025 county taxes keep accruing interest and fees.
  • Payment plans may be available for certain residential, owner-occupied property, case by case.

Scammers target owners in foreclosure. Neither the county nor its attorneys will ask for gift cards, cryptocurrency, wire transfers or online banking logins. Free help is available from the state Attorney General's Homeowner Protection Program at 1-855-HOME-456.

sections.h2: Housing and taxes across the county
sections.html:
About 946,741 people live in Erie County, and roughly 65.8 percent of homes are owner-occupied. The typical home is valued at $233,800 and the typical rent is $1,090. The county has 16 villages, including Williamsville, Hamburg, Kenmore, East Aurora and Orchard Park, and school districts range from Buffalo City to small central districts such as Holland and Akron. Tax bills therefore vary by town, village and district.

Interest is added on the first of every month, so mark the redemption date in each in rem notice on a calendar. Notices also go to mortgage holders and others with an interest in the parcel, and those recipients are advised to speak with an attorney to protect their position.

sections.h2: Does STAR work differently in Buffalo?
sections.html:
Yes. STAR applies only to school district taxes, with five cities as exceptions: New York, Buffalo, Rochester, Yonkers and Syracuse. In those cities the benefit is applied partly to city taxes and partly to school taxes. A Buffalo homeowner and a Lancaster homeowner can therefore see the benefit land on different lines of the bill.

The credit comes as a check or direct deposit. The older STAR exemption on the bill continues only for owners who have held it since 2015 on the same home, and new homeowners register for the credit. Basic STAR has a $500,000 income limit, and Enhanced STAR for owners aged 65 and over needs income of $110,750 or less for the 2026-2027 school year.

Work out which level of government you owe, because the answers come from different offices. County liens near foreclosure sit with RPTS. Current town and school tax sits with the town receiver. The RPTS online system shows county amounts, and the tax line at (716) 858-8333 can give an exact payoff.

  1. Look up the parcel on the county's payment site and note every open year, since foreclosure eligibility turns on liens at least two years old.
  2. If the parcel appears on a foreclosure list, find the last day of redemption and the answer deadline in the notice you received.
  3. Call RPTS to ask whether a payment plan is possible for an owner-occupied home.
  4. Pass the payoff figures to your closing attorney so the lien is cleared at or before closing.

A cash buyer can close quickly and pay the lien from proceeds, which stops further monthly interest. Collect the figure in writing and ask that it be good through your closing date.

A notice is not a bill, and it is worth reading line by line. It states the last day to redeem and the deadline to answer, and it names the lien years covered. Because interest is added on the first day of each month, the amount shown is only good until that date, so ask RPTS for an updated payoff before you send anything. The foreclosure fee goes in a separate check, and payment must be by cash, certified check, bank check or money order.

Mortgage holders and others with an interest in the parcel receive the same notice. If you own the house with someone else or have a lender, find out who is responding so that no one assumes the other is handling it.

sections.h2: What a cash sale can do for a lien
sections.html:
Erie County owners often come to a sale because tax liens, interest and fees have piled up over several years. A cash purchase can pay the county from the proceeds at closing, which stops monthly interest and keeps later years from becoming eligible for foreclosure. We buy houses as-is, so you do not need to repair anything first, and you owe nothing if you decline an offer.

The practical steps are short. Ask RPTS for the payoff, ask your town receiver about any current bill, and share both figures with us. We include them in the written offer, and the title company pays each office when the deed is recorded. If a payment plan is available for your owner-occupied home, you can compare it with a sale and choose the path that suits you.

If a house has already been sold at auction, the former owner may be owed surplus money. The claimant files a Notice of Claim in the County Clerk's Office and starts a legal proceeding on notice to others with an interest. A lawyer is not required. A judge decides who receives what. The County Comptroller, at (716) 858-8400, holds the surplus.

Free counseling and legal help are available. The New York State Attorney General's Homeowner Protection Program, at 1-855-HOME-456, connects owners to housing counselors and attorneys at no charge. Avoid anyone who charges a fee to guarantee foreclosure relief. If you have received an in rem notice, read the redemption and answer deadlines first, then call RPTS before doing anything else.

faqs.q: How long must an Erie County tax lien go unpaid before foreclosure?
faqs.a: Two years or more. In Rem 173 covered liens through tax year 2022.

faqs.q: How much is the Erie County foreclosure fee?
faqs.a: $500, paid on top of the unpaid liens and interest. It should be issued as a separate check.

faqs.q: Can I pay Erie County delinquent tax online?
faqs.a: Yes. The county's online system accepts delinquent Erie County property taxes for any town or city in the county, and current county tax for the City of Buffalo. Current bills elsewhere go to the town receiver.

faqs.q: Is there an Erie County foreclosure auction coming up?
faqs.a: Call RPTS at (716) 858-8333 for the next sale schedule and the status of In Rem 174.

faqs.q: Who helps Erie County owners facing tax foreclosure for free?
faqs.a: The New York State Attorney General's Homeowner Protection Program, at 1-855-HOME-456, connects owners to free housing counseling or legal help. Avoid anyone who charges a fee to guarantee foreclosure relief.
